_meta.title: The cavities the qubits already touch are two-qubit buses: J through the shared readout (and drive) cavity vs the unmanufacturable tens-of-aF C_qq
_meta.rng: none -- no stochastic step; no seed is used or needed
_meta.claim_discipline: DESIGN STUDY. Every coherence number is parametric in x_qp or in the 1/f amplitude A. No absolute TBG T1/T2 and no gate fidelity is claimed: the error entries are leading-order INCOHERENT BUDGET CONTRIBUTIONS, not simulated fidelities.
reads: qubit/ (spectrum, dome, cavity, coupling, noise_1f, qp_kernel, inputs)

A_1f.units: filling nu per e-fold, S_nu(w) = A^2/|w| two-sided

dnu_set.meaning: rms gate-setting error on the parking filling

IR_cutoff.note: P4 convention, 1 s acquisition; T2 apex is the most IR-sensitive number in the export

readout_bus.t_convention: t_iSWAP = 1/(2J), the convention already used in qubit.json:two_qubit_sketch (J = 15.611 MHz -> 32.028 ns). NOTE: the brief's '0.8-1.0 us' drive-bus figure corresponds instead to 1/(4J); the repo convention is kept here and gives 1.58-1.99 us.

dispersive_headroom.statement: J_bus/D = 0.0174 against the sketch's 0.1 dispersive criterion: the readout bus sits 5.75x INSIDE the budget that forced C_qq <= 18.6 aF

combined_bus.statement: the two buses are NOT alternatives: every island is capacitively attached to both cavities, so J_total = J_ro + J_dr always. The drive cavity adds 6.3% to the readout bus at the stored 20 um electrode and CANNOT be switched off either.

drive_electrode_upgrade.idea: the drive electrode is the cheapest unused resource on the island: g ~ C_c * d_eff ~ d_eff^2 so J_dr ~ d_eff^4, while the bus Purcell error pi kappa_d/Delta_d does NOT depend on g

constraints.C_c_model: coupling.c_c_selfcap: C_c = kappa_geo eps0 eps_eff d_eff

no_readout_verdict_survives.statement: even with the largest drive electrode the budget allows, chi/kappa through the 145 GHz cavity stays far below 1: the P2/P5 'the drive cavity cannot read the qubit out' verdict is robust to this upgrade

drive_electrode_upgrade.caveats: d_eff_drive = 20 um is a STORED photonics input; changing it is a design proposal, not a measured value. It would require re-running P2's divider and P5's control-line budget, and it pushes the lumped pickup from lambda/30 to lambda/13 at 145 GHz. Reported as a parametric extension, not a result.

drive_bus.pair_breaking_note: the drive cavity is the 145 GHz mode whose pair-breaking window DEFINES the nu range used here; using it as a bus adds no new tone and no new pair-breaking exposure (qubit.json:open_items.photon_assisted_pair_breaking still applies unchanged).

purcell_structural_floor.identity: t_iSWAP/T1_Purcell = [1/(2J)] (g/D)^2 2 pi kappa = pi kappa / D  with J = g^2/D -- g cancels

absolute_Q_i_floor.derivation: kappa >= f_bus/Q_i (constraint C2) => the two-qubit Purcell error of ANY cavity-bus iSWAP on this platform is 2 pi kappa/D >= 2 pi (1 + f01/D)/Q_i, which tends to 2 pi/Q_i as the bus detuning grows. g, d_eff, beta and C_c all cancel.

off_state_cost.reference_note: 100 ns = one readout-bus iSWAP = 62 single-qubit gates at the honest 1.6044 ns floor
off_state_cost.finding: THE BINDING RESULT. The nu-window is not a usable on/off knob for the readout bus: suppressing the residual swap requires parking a qubit far enough off-apex that its own echo coherence collapses, and the two costs cross at a floor of 0.083 per 100 ns of idling. The 22x weaker drive bus reaches 1.37e-02 at the same knob, because its residual swap is already negligible at small splits.

apex_law.criterion: for every one of the 1681 parkings, moving the INNER qubit to nu = -2.4 leaves min(T2_echo) unchanged and does not reduce the split: zero violations means the apex family weakly dominates
apex_law.statement: because f01(nu) is EVEN about the apex, the split depends only on (|nu1+2.4|, |nu2+2.4|) while the coherence cost |D1| grows monotonically with each; so for every reachable split the Pareto-optimal parking puts ONE qubit exactly at the apex and pays the whole coherence bill on the other. The evenness flagged as a liability in allocation.degeneracy_note is what makes the ON state (both at the apex) EXACTLY degenerate with no fine tuning.

stray_direct_C_qq.sign_note: both cavities sit ABOVE f01 (Delta_r = +4.0 GHz, Delta_d = +104.4 GHz), so J_bus > 0 and adds to the direct capacitive J; a readout mode placed BELOW f01 would subtract and could cancel the stray -- an unexplored design knob.

measurement_conflict.statement: a SHARED readout cavity gives one joint dispersive shift: the pull is chi_1 n_1 + chi_2 n_2, so |01> and |10> are separated only by |chi_1 - chi_2|. Per-qubit readout needs the FDM neighbour cavity -- NOT modelled here.
measurement_conflict.verdict: the largest chi split reachable inside the fixed-drive window is smaller than the cavity linewidth, so ONE shared readout cavity measures only the total excitation number of the pair

addressability.statement: the fork verdict 'EXACTLY 1 qubit' is about FREQUENCY-selective driving and it is unchanged here: 0.2906 GHz of span against a measured 0.9235 GHz minimum spacing even at t_g = 8 ns. A bus does not repair that. Two bus-coupled islands therefore need SPATIALLY separate drive ports; what the bus removes is the coupler fab tolerance, not the addressing requirement.

V3a_ZZ_formula_vs_direct_exchange_diag.regime: two transmons, 4 levels each, direct exchange J, no cavity

V3b_ZZ_cavity_diag_vs_pure_exchange.finding: the cavity bus produces LESS static ZZ than a direct exchange of the same strength: the measured factor at Delta_r = 4 GHz is 0.5919, i.e. a 40.8% cancellation, and the Delta_r sweep below shows it converging to 1 as 1 - |alpha|/Delta

V5_per_island_C_Sigma_budget.statement: each island carries its own C_Sigma = 12.99971 fF and its own pair of collection electrodes; the CAVITY is shared, the BUDGET is not. Two islands therefore spend 8.70101 fF each against an 11.99971 fF cap, exactly as the single-qubit recommended point does -- no shared-budget violation, and 3.29870 fF of headroom per island remains. A direct C_qq would instead spend from BOTH budgets simultaneously.
V5_per_island_C_Sigma_budget.budget_law: C_Sigma is LOCKED at 12.99971 fF by E_J/E_C = 100, so the collection electrode SPENDS that budget rather than adding to it: C_c <= C_Sigma - C_J and beta_max = 1 - C_J/C_Sigma

verdict.headline: The readout cavity IS a two-qubit bus and it replaces the unmanufacturable capacitor: J_ro = 5.0507 MHz, t_iSWAP = 98.996 ns, equivalent to a direct C_qq of 3.2353 aF -- 5.74x BELOW the 18.576 aF dispersive cap the sketch demanded, i.e. inside the budget with room to spare and with zero fab tolerance, because it is set by a cavity that has already been measured. What the bus does NOT provide is an off switch: the 0.2906 GHz nu window is the only knob and it cannot suppress the residual swap without parking a qubit where its own echo coherence collapses.

readout_bus.coupler_verdict: J, dispersive headroom, ZZ and the per-gate error budget are all acceptable
readout_bus.switch_verdict: the nu-window on/off knob floors the idle cost at 0.0827 per 100 ns; a tunable coupler or a compiled always-on scheme is required
readout_bus.on_state_is_protected: both islands at nu = -2.4: f01 degenerate EXACTLY by the evenness of the dome, and D1 = 0 makes the resonance condition first-order insensitive to gate-setting noise (swap error 0 at dnu_rms = 1e-3, vs 0.2001 for a symmetric parking at nu = -2.3707)
readout_bus.binding_constraint: Purcell through the SAME cavity that provides the coupling: t_g/T1_P = pi kappa_r/Delta_r with g cancelled = 2.710e-03

drive_bus.grade: NOT VIABLE at the stored 20 um drive electrode
drive_bus.why_not: t_iSWAP = 1.5799 us is longer than everything: the READOUT cavity's own Purcell background (36.54 us) runs during the drive-bus gate and alone costs 8.7e-2, and the quasiparticle channel adds 5.7e-2 at x_qp = 1e-7. The isolation is excellent (P_off = 4.70e-6) but the gate is too slow to use it.
drive_bus.binding_constraint: quasiparticle T1 over the 1.6-2.0 us gate

drive_bus_upgraded_electrode.grade: LOWEST GATE ERROR ON CHIP, but it moves a stored photonics input (d_eff_drive 20 -> 47.25 um) and needs a P2/P5 re-run
drive_bus_upgraded_electrode.ZZ_cost: static ZZ scales as J^2 so the faster bus carries more of it: 232.3 kHz at the maximum split vs 33.9 kHz for the readout bus, i.e. 3.5x more conditional phase per gate
drive_bus_upgraded_electrode.caveat: d_eff_drive = 20 um is a STORED photonics input; changing it is a design proposal, not a measured value. It would require re-running P2's divider and P5's control-line budget, and it pushes the lumped pickup from lambda/30 to lambda/13 at 145 GHz. Reported as a parametric extension, not a result.

direct_C_qq_at_cap.why: every term in the budget is proportional to t_g, so the bus costs exactly the gate-time ratio J_cap/J_bus = 5.74x more decoherence per gate than a perfect direct capacitor at its dispersive cap -- and buys away the entire fab tolerance
